symbols.name: d
symbols.def: A probability law selected before outcomes are observed.

symbols.name: z
symbols.def: The assignment drawn from \(d\), with \(z_i=+1\) for treatment and \(z_i=-1\) for control.

symbols.name: treatment_label
symbols.def: A label indexing the two fixed potential outcomes.

symbols.name: Y_i_obs
symbols.def: The outcome recorded for unit \(i\) after the assignment is drawn.

symbols.name: mu
symbols.def: Let \(m_i=\{y_i(1)+y_i(0)\}/2\); then \(\mu=P_Hm\in H_n\) is its centered component.

symbols.name: S
symbols.space: \(\{L:L\text{ is a linear subspace of }H_n,\ 1\leq\dim L\leq n-1\}\)
symbols.def: The span generated from the external prognostic score matrix after centering, known before assignment.

symbols.name: rho
symbols.def: A free parameter indexing the oracle class through the restriction \(\rho_{\mu}(S)\geq\rho\); it is not a functional of the score matrix.

symbols.name: rho_star_S
symbols.def: \(\rho^*(S)=\inf\{\rho\in[0,1]:V^*(\rho;S)<V_{\mathrm{CRD}}(\rho;S)\}\), with value \(1\) when the set is empty.

symbols.name: d_reg
symbols.def: A design selected without committing to a value of the free lower-bound index \(\rho\) and evaluated by additive oracle regret.

symbols.name: d_pair_4
symbols.def: The law assigning probability \(1/4\) to each element of \(\{\pm(1,-1,1,-1)^\top,\ \pm(1,-1,-1,1)^\top\}\).

assumptions.condition: The array \(\{y_i(0),y_i(1):i=1,\ldots,n\}\) is fixed with respect to the assignment law \(d\).

definitions.name: Exact balanced covariance hull
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_n=\operatorname{conv}\{zz^\top:z\in\mathcal Z_n\}\), represented by weights on sign-pairs \(\{z,-z\}\).

definitions.name: Realized score quality
definitions.construction: For each specified nonzero \(\mu\in H_n\), \(\rho_{\mu}(S)=\|P_S\mu\|_2/\|\mu\|_2\); the free oracle index \(\rho\in[0,1]\) imposes the lower-bound condition \(\rho_{\mu}(S)\geq\rho\).

definitions.name: Admissibility and threshold invariants
definitions.construction: \(\kappa(S)=\min_{A\in\mathcal C_n}\lambda_{\max}(P_SAP_S\mid S)\) and \(\gamma(S)=\inf_{A\in\mathcal C_n,\eta>0}\{\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-c_n\}/\eta\).

definitions.name: Spectral-breakpoint regret handle
definitions.construction: Parameterize quality by \(s=\rho^2\); use the scalar dual \(\min_{\eta\geq0}\{\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-\eta s\}\), the balanced-cut-hull support oracle, and the eigenvalue-crossing breakpoints of the resulting upper envelopes to construct a finite epigraph for the target \(R^*(n,S)\) and a covariance for \(d_{\mathrm{reg}}\).

definitions.name: Four-unit score basis and balanced sign-pair mixture
definitions.construction: Set \(u_4=2^{-1}(1,1,-1,-1)^\top\) and \(S_4=\operatorname{span}\{u_4\}\). Define \(d_{\mathrm{pair},4}\) by probability \(1/4\) on each assignment in \(\{\pm(1,-1,1,-1)^\top,\ \pm(1,-1,-1,1)^\top\}\); its covariance is \(A_{\mathrm{pair},4}=\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&0&0\\-1&1&0&0\\0&0&1&-1\\0&0&-1&1\end{pmatrix}\).

statements.statement: For every \(d\in\mathcal D_n\), the estimator \(\widehat\tau_d\) is design-unbiased for \(\tau_n\) and obeys \[\mathbb E_d[(\widehat\tau_d-\tau_n)^2]=\frac{4}{n^2}\mu^\top A_d\mu.\]
statements.justification: This identity turns the design problem into an exact quadratic-risk problem with assignment as the only source of randomness.
statements.gap: HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024, Lemma 1, gives the corresponding covariance identity; the present lemma fixes the balanced difference-in-means normalization used by the new oracle.
statements.consumer: The exact value, admissibility frontier, and regret statements all use this equality to translate their covariance criteria into SATE mean squared error.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(m_i=\{y_i(1)+y_i(0)\}/2\) and \(\delta_i=y_i(1)-y_i(0)\).  The potential outcomes are fixed by Assumption \(\text{ass:fixed-potential-outcomes}\), so all expectations below are with respect to the assignment alone.  Assumption \(\text{ass:consistency-no-interference}\) and \(z_i\in\{-1,1\}\) give, identically for every supported assignment,
\[
Y_i^{\mathrm{obs}}=m_i+\frac{z_i\delta_i}{2}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\widehat\tau_d
=\frac{2}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n z_i m_i+\frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n z_i^2\delta_i
=\tau_n+\frac{2}{n}z^\top m.
\]
Every \(z\in\mathcal Z_n\) is orthogonal to \(\mathbf 1_n\).  Since \(\mu=P_Hm\), this implies \(z^\top m=z^\top\mu\), and hence
\[
\widehat\tau_d-\tau_n=\frac{2}{n}z^\top\mu.
\]
The defining mean-zero condition in \(\mathcal D_n\) yields \(\mathbb E_d[z]=0\).  Thus \(\mathbb E_d[\widehat\tau_d]=\tau_n\).  It also implies \(A_d=\mathbb E_d[zz^\top]\), and therefore
\[
\mathbb E_d[(\widehat\tau_d-\tau_n)^2]
=\frac{4}{n^2}\mathbb E_d[\mu^\top zz^\top\mu]
=\frac{4}{n^2}\mu^\top A_d\mu.
\]
Finally, because each \(z_i\) is binary and has mean zero, \(\Pr_d(z_i=1)=\Pr_d(z_i=-1)=1/2\).  Thus the marginal exposure probabilities used by the unbiasedness calculation are positive; no superpopulation or outcome randomness has been introduced.

statements.statement: The covariance image of \(\mathcal D_n\) is exactly \(\mathcal C_n\): \[\{A_d:d\in\mathcal D_n\}=\operatorname{conv}\{zz^\top:z\in\mathcal Z_n\}.\] In particular, every convex representation can be symmetrized over \(\{z,-z\}\) to yield a mean-zero attaining design without changing its covariance.
statements.justification: This is the implementability bridge that rules out fictitious positive-semidefinite covariance solutions.
statements.gap: HuberMaric2019, p. 5, Theorem 2, characterizes symmetric Bernoulli correlations through the cut polytope, but does not impose the fixed-treatment-count support \(\mathcal Z_n\) or connect it to SATE risk.
statements.consumer: An experimenter can convert every optimizer in the later finite program into an actual balanced randomization distribution.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(d\in\mathcal D_n\).  Its support is contained in the finite set \(\mathcal Z_n\), and its mean is zero.  Hence
\[
A_d=\mathbb E_d[zz^\top]
=\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}d(z)zz^\top
\in\operatorname{conv}\{zz^\top:z\in\mathcal Z_n\}=\mathcal C_n.
\]
This proves one inclusion.

Conversely, take \(A\in\mathcal C_n\) and a convex representation
\[
A=\sum_{j=1}^J a_j z^{(j)}z^{(j)\top},
\qquad a_j\geq0,\quad \sum_{j=1}^J a_j=1,
\quad z^{(j)}\in\mathcal Z_n.
\]
Define a law by putting mass \(a_j/2\) at each of \(z^{(j)}\) and \(-z^{(j)}\), combining masses when assignments repeat.  The set \(\mathcal Z_n\) is closed under sign reversal because \(n\) is even and every supported vector is balanced.  The resulting law has mean
\[
\sum_{j=1}^J\frac{a_j}{2}\{z^{(j)}-z^{(j)}\}=0,
\]
so it belongs to \(\mathcal D_n\), while its covariance is
\[
\sum_{j=1}^J\frac{a_j}{2}
\{z^{(j)}z^{(j)\top}+(-z^{(j)})(-z^{(j)})^\top\}=A.
\]
Thus every point of the cut hull is implementable by an actual balanced, mean-zero randomization, proving the reverse inclusion and the stated symmetrization claim.

statements.statement: For every \(A\in\mathcal C_n\) and \(\rho\in[0,1]\), the nonconvex spherical-shell adversary has the rank-one-exact lift and scalar dual \[q_\rho(A;S)=\max_{X\in\mathcal X_\rho(S)}\operatorname{tr}(AX)=\min_{\eta\geq0}\left\{\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-\eta\rho^2\right\}.\] Moreover, the lifted maximum admits a rank-one optimizer.
statements.justification: The exact lift is the technical move that makes the quality cone solvable without relaxing away its worst-case outcome vector.
statements.gap: Kallus2018OptimalBalance and Kallus2021Randomization reduce ellipsoidal classes to largest eigenvalues; no located result supplies this exact two-constraint lift for a lower score-energy shell.
statements.consumer: The dual exposes score quality as a scalar slope and yields both the critical-quality formula and the regret breakpoint handle.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(s=\rho^2\) and let
\[
K_s=\{X\succeq0:X=P_HXP_H,\ \operatorname{tr}(X)=1,
\ \operatorname{tr}(P_SX)\geq s\}=\mathcal X_\rho(S).
\]
This set is nonempty and compact: a rank-one projector onto any unit vector in \(S\) belongs to it.  Every feasible unit vector \(u\) in the definition of \(q_\rho(A;S)\) gives the feasible rank-one matrix \(X=uu^\top\), with \(\operatorname{tr}(AX)=u^\top Au\).

We next prove that a linear functional on \(K_s\) has a rank-one maximizer.  A maximizer may be chosen to be an extreme point because \(K_s\) is compact and convex.  Suppose an extreme point \(X\) had rank \(r\geq2\), and let \(R=\operatorname{range}(X)\subseteq H_n\).  The vector space of symmetric operators on \(R\) has dimension \(r(r+1)/2\geq3\).  If the score constraint is active, choose a nonzero symmetric operator \(D\), supported on \(R\), satisfying
\[
\operatorname{tr}(D)=0,
\qquad \operatorname{tr}(P_SD)=0;
\]
such a \(D\) exists because these are at most two homogeneous linear equations.  If the score constraint is inactive, impose only \(\operatorname{tr}(D)=0\).  Since \(X\) is positive definite on \(R\), for all sufficiently small \(\epsilon>0\), both \(X+\epsilon D\) and \(X-\epsilon D\) are positive semidefinite.  They retain the support and trace constraints; in the active case they retain score energy exactly, and in the inactive case feasibility persists by strict slack and continuity.  Hence \(X\) is the midpoint of two distinct feasible matrices, a contradiction.  Every extreme point therefore has rank one.  A rank-one member of \(K_s\) is \(uu^\top\) for a unit \(u\in H_n\) satisfying \(u^\top P_Su\geq s\).  This proves
\[
q_\rho(A;S)=\max_{X\in\mathcal X_\rho(S)}\operatorname{tr}(AX)
\]
and proves the claimed rank-one attainment.

For the scalar dual, attach a multiplier \(\eta\geq0\) to \(\operatorname{tr}(P_SX)-s\geq0\).  Maximizing the Lagrangian over positive semidefinite trace-one operators on \(H_n\) gives
\[
\max_{X\succeq0,\ X=P_HXP_H,\ \operatorname{tr}(X)=1}
\operatorname{tr}\{(A+\eta P_S)X\}-\eta s
=\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-\eta s.
\]
For \(s<1\), there is a positive definite density operator on \(H_n\) whose score trace is strictly larger than \(s\): put sufficiently large mass on \(S\) and a positive amount on its orthogonal complement, with the evident simplification when \(S=H_n\).  Finite-dimensional separating-hyperplane duality therefore has no gap, yielding the displayed infimum over \(\eta\geq0\).

It remains to check the boundary \(s=1\), where strict feasibility is unavailable.  Positive semidefiniteness and
\(\operatorname{tr}(P_SX)=\operatorname{tr}(X)=1\) force \(X=P_SXP_S\), so the primal value is
\(\lambda_{\max}(P_SAP_S\mid S)\).  Relative to the orthogonal decomposition \(H_n=S\oplus(H_n\cap S^\perp)\), the largest eigenvalue of \(A+\eta P_S\), minus \(\eta\), converges as \(\eta\to\infty\) to \(\lambda_{\max}(P_SAP_S\mid S)\).  This follows directly from the Rayleigh quotient: maximizing vectors with a nonvanishing complementary component lose order \(\eta\) after subtraction, while vectors in \(S\) give the compressed Rayleigh quotient.  Weak duality gives the reverse inequality for every finite \(\eta\).  Thus the dual equality also holds at \(s=1\), possibly with its infimum attained only in the limit \(\eta=\infty\).

statements.statement: For every \(\rho\in[0,1]\), \[v^*(\rho;S)=\min_{A\in\mathcal C_n}\max_{X\in\mathcal X_\rho(S)}\operatorname{tr}(AX)=\max_{X\in\mathcal X_\rho(S)}\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}z^\top Xz.\] Equivalently, \(v^*(\rho;S)\) is the optimum of \[\max_{X,t}\ t\quad\text{subject to}\quad X\in\mathcal X_\rho(S),\quad t\leq z^\top Xz\ \text{for every }z\in\mathcal Z_n.\] The dual yields weights on balanced sign-pairs defining an attaining \(d^*_{\rho,S}\in\mathcal D_n\), and every \(d\in\mathcal D_n\) satisfies \[\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal Y(\rho,M;S)}\mathbb E_d[(\widehat\tau_d-\tau_n)^2]\geq V^*(\rho;S),\] with equality for \(d^*_{\rho,S}\).
statements.justification: This is the exact design and matching converse over the full discrete design class, not an elliptope relaxation or a candidate procedure.
statements.gap: Kallus2021Randomization, Section 5, identifies the generic mixed-strategy optimal design for a specified conditional-mean class. The theorem-level delta here is the solution of the nonellipsoidal lower score-energy shell: a rank-one-exact lift, an explicit finite saddle value over the balanced cut hull, sign-pair recovery of an attaining design, and a matching converse over every balanced mean-zero law. HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 instead provides bounds for one named design.
statements.consumer: Trial designers with an externally trained score can enumerate or column-generate the oracle assignment mixture and report a certified worst-case SATE risk.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\rho\in[0,1]\) and abbreviate \(\mathcal X_\rho(S)\) by \(K\).  Both \(K\) and \(\mathcal C_n\) are nonempty compact convex sets, and \((A,X)\mapsto\operatorname{tr}(AX)\) is bilinear.  For completeness, the needed minimax equality can be seen by a finite separation argument.  Enumerate the balanced sign-pairs by representatives \(z^{(1)},\ldots,z^{(m)}\), and put \(g_j(X)=z^{(j)\top}Xz^{(j)}\).  If
\(r>\max_{X\in K}\min_j g_j(X)\), then the compact convex image
\[
\{(g_1(X)-r,\ldots,g_m(X)-r):X\in K\}
\]
is disjoint from the nonnegative orthant.  Strong separation supplies a nonzero nonnegative vector \(a\); after normalization \(a\in\Delta_m\), and
\[
\max_{X\in K}\sum_{j=1}^m a_jg_j(X)<r.
\]
Letting \(r\) decrease to the right-hand max--min value proves the reverse of the elementary weak-minimax inequality.  Consequently,
\[
\min_{a\in\Delta_m}\max_{X\in K}
\sum_{j=1}^m a_jz^{(j)\top}Xz^{(j)}
=\max_{X\in K}\min_{1\leq j\leq m}z^{(j)\top}Xz^{(j)}.
\]
The left side is \(\min_{A\in\mathcal C_n}\max_{X\in K}\operatorname{tr}(AX)\), and sign reversal does not change the right side.  The cone-lift theorem and the definition of \(v^*(\rho;S)\) now give the first display in the theorem.

Introducing a scalar \(t\), the identity
\[
t\leq\min_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}z^\top Xz
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
t\leq z^\top Xz\ \text{for every }z\in\mathcal Z_n
\]
gives the stated finite semidefinite program.  Compactness gives primal and minimizing covariance optimizers.  The separating vector \(a\), equivalently the dual weights for the finitely many cut constraints, represents an optimizing covariance as a convex combination of \(z^{(j)}z^{(j)\top}\).  By balanced-covariance realizability, symmetrizing these weights produces an attaining design \(d^*_{\rho,S}\in\mathcal D_n\).

It remains to translate the spectral game into causal mean squared error.  For any \(\mu\in\mathcal Y(\rho,M;S)\), write \(\mu=\sqrt{nM}\,u\).  Then \(u\in H_n\), \(\|u\|_2=1\), and \(u^\top P_Su\geq\rho^2\).  The exact design-risk lemma and the rank-one-exact lift yield, for every \(d\in\mathcal D_n\),
\[
\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal Y(\rho,M;S)}
\mathbb E_d[(\widehat\tau_d-\tau_n)^2]
=\frac{4M}{n}q_\rho(A_d;S)
\geq\frac{4M}{n}v^*(\rho;S)=V^*(\rho;S).
\]
For the symmetrized design whose covariance minimizes the game, equality holds.  Thus the causal target remains the fixed SATE \(\tau_n\); \(V^*(\rho;S)\) is the exact design-risk criterion for its unbiased estimator, not a redefinition of that causal estimand.

statements.statement: The following conditions are equivalent: \[(i)\ S\in\mathfrak A_n,\qquad (ii)\ \kappa(S)<c_n,\qquad (iii)\ \gamma(S)<1.\] When these conditions hold, \[\rho^*(S)=\sqrt{\gamma(S)};\] otherwise \(\rho^*(S)=1\). Given a basis matrix for \(S\) and a tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), enumeration of \(\mathcal Z_n\), semidefinite optimization, and one-dimensional bisection compute \(\kappa(S)\), \(\rho^*(S)\), and an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal attaining assignment mixture using only the score matrix and \(n\).
statements.justification: The theorem answers exactly when an external score justifies any restriction before perfect prediction and locates the first quality level at which it does.
statements.gap: HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 does not classify score geometries, Bai2022MatchedPairs handles a scalar prognosis within stratified schemes, and HuberMaric2019 has no score-compressed spectral objective.
statements.consumer: A protocol author can decide from the pre-randomization score matrix whether a restricted design has any certified minimax advantage over complete randomization.
statements.proof_tex:
Set \(s=\rho^2\).  Since every \(A\in\mathcal C_n\) is a convex combination of matrices \(zz^\top\), it is positive semidefinite, annihilates \(\mathbf 1_n\), has diagonal entries one, and has trace \(n\).  On the \((n-1)\)-dimensional space \(H_n\), therefore,
\[
\lambda_{\max}(A\mid H_n)\geq\frac{\operatorname{tr}(A)}{n-1}
=\frac{n}{n-1}=c_n.
\]
Complete randomization has covariance \(c_nP_H\), so its normalized worst-case risk is exactly \(c_n\) at every quality level.

At perfect quality, the feasible unit vectors lie in \(S\), and hence
\[
q_1(A;S)=\lambda_{\max}(P_SAP_S\mid S),
\qquad v^*(1;S)=\kappa(S).
\]
If improvement occurs at some \(s<1\), then for its witnessing covariance \(A\),
\[
\kappa(S)\leq q_1(A;S)\leq q_{\sqrt{s}}(A;S)<c_n.
\]
Conversely, suppose \(\kappa(S)<c_n\) and choose an attaining \(A_0\).  As \(s\uparrow1\), the compact feasible spherical sets decrease to the unit sphere in \(S\), so
\[
q_{\sqrt{s}}(A_0;S)\longrightarrow q_1(A_0;S)=\kappa(S).
\]
To verify this limit without an unstated continuity assumption, take maximizers along any sequence \(s_j\uparrow1\), pass to a convergent subsequence on the unit sphere, and observe that the limit has score energy one and hence lies in \(S\).  Thus \(q_{\sqrt{s}}(A_0;S)<c_n\) for some \(s<1\).  This proves
\[
S\in\mathfrak A_n\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\kappa(S)<c_n.
\]

The scalar dual gives the threshold exactly.  Because the value at \(\eta=0\) is at least \(c_n\), strict improvement satisfies
\[
v^*(\sqrt{s};S)<c_n
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\text{there exist }A\in\mathcal C_n\text{ and }\eta>0\text{ such that }
\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-\eta s<c_n.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
v^*(\sqrt{s};S)<c_n
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
s>inf_{A\in\mathcal C_n,\,\eta>0}
\frac{\lambda_{\max}(A+\eta P_S\mid H_n)-c_n}{\eta}
=\gamma(S).
\]
The numerator is nonnegative because adding \(\eta P_S\succeq0\) cannot reduce the largest eigenvalue below \(c_n\); hence \(\gamma(S)\geq0\).  Complete randomization gives quotient one for every \(\eta>0\), so \(\gamma(S)\leq1\).  It follows that improvement at some \(s<1\) is equivalent to \(\gamma(S)<1\), and, in that case, the improving squared-quality set is exactly \((\gamma(S),1]\).  Therefore its infimum in the original quality coordinate is
\[
\rho^*(S)=\sqrt{\gamma(S)}.
\]
If \(\gamma(S)=1\), the improvement set is empty and the stipulated value is \(1\).  Combining this with the preceding equivalence proves all three parts of the dichotomy.

We finally make computability explicit.  Enumerate one representative from each sign-pair in \(\mathcal Z_n\), say \(z^{(1)},\ldots,z^{(m)}\), and write
\(A(a)=\sum_{j=1}^m a_jz^{(j)}z^{(j)\top}\) for \(a\in\Delta_m\).  If \(Q_S\) is an orthonormal basis matrix for \(S\), then \(\kappa(S)\) is the finite semidefinite program
\[
\min_{a\in\Delta_m,\,t}\ t
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
tI_{\dim S}-Q_S^\top A(a)Q_S\succeq0.
\]
For fixed \(s\), the strict-improvement test is the one-scalar semidefinite feasibility condition
\[
a\in\Delta_m,\quad \eta>0,
\qquad (c_n+\eta s)I_{n-1}-Q_H^\top\{A(a)+\eta P_S\}Q_H\succ0,
\]
where \(Q_H\) is any orthonormal basis matrix for \(H_n\).  The test is monotone in \(s\), so bisection on \([0,1]\), with non-strict semidefinite bounds at the boundary, computes \(\gamma(S)\) and hence \(\rho^*(S)\) to any prescribed tolerance.  At a requested \(\rho\), the finite saddle program in the exact-oracle theorem and its finite dual compute an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal covariance and sign-pair weights.  Symmetrization produces the corresponding assignment mixture.  All matrices in these programs are obtained from \(n\), the centered score basis, and the enumerated balanced assignments; neither outcomes nor the unknown realized quality enter.

statements.statement: If \(S=H_n\), then \(v^*(\rho;S)=c_n\) for every \(\rho\in[0,1]\), so \(S\notin\mathfrak A_n\). For the worked \(n=4\) basis \(u_4=2^{-1}(1,1,-1,-1)^\top\) and \(S_4=\operatorname{span}\{u_4\}=S_{\mathrm{pair}}\), the displayed balanced sign-pair mixture \(d_{\mathrm{pair},4}\) has covariance \(A_{\mathrm{pair},4}\) and satisfies \[v^*(\rho;S_4)=\min\left\{\frac43,\ 2(1-\rho^2)\right\},\qquad \kappa(S_4)=0,\qquad \gamma(S_4)=\frac13,\qquad \rho^*(S_4)=\frac1{\sqrt3}.\] Complete randomization attains the first branch for \(\rho\leq1/\sqrt3\), while \(d_{\mathrm{pair},4}\) attains the second branch for \(\rho\geq1/\sqrt3\). More generally, independent fair orientations within fixed pairs give \(\kappa(S_{\mathrm{pair}})=0\), so \(S_{\mathrm{pair}}\in\mathfrak A_n\). At \(n=8\) and \(M=1\), \(V^*(1;S_{\mathrm{pair}})=0\) while \(V_{\mathrm{CRD}}(1;S_{\mathrm{pair}})=4/7\).
statements.justification: These reductions pin both sides of the dichotomy, compute the full four-unit frontier from an explicit score basis and implementable sign-pair mixture, and reproduce the exact enumerated eight-unit endpoint.
statements.gap: Bai2022MatchedPairs establishes a superpopulation stratified optimum, whereas this proposition is a fixed-population reduction inside the unrestricted balanced assignment class.
statements.consumer: The closed-form four-unit calculation provides a reproducible unit test for the cut-hull solver and shows a protocol author exactly how the threshold changes the attaining design.
statements.proof_tex:
First take \(S=H_n\).  The score constraint is then automatic at every \(\rho\), so \(q_\rho(A;H_n)=\lambda_{\max}(A\mid H_n)\).  Every \(A\in\mathcal C_n\) has trace \(n\) on the \((n-1)\)-dimensional space \(H_n\), whence \(\lambda_{\max}(A\mid H_n)\geq c_n\).  Complete randomization has covariance \(c_nP_H\) and attains equality.  Thus \(v^*(\rho;H_n)=c_n\) for all \(\rho\), and no strict improvement is possible.

For \(n=4\), supplement \(u_4\) by
\[
v_4=\frac12(1,-1,1,-1)^\top,
\qquad w_4=\frac12(1,-1,-1,1)^\top.
\]
These three vectors form an orthonormal basis of \(H_4\).  Up to sign, the three balanced assignments are \(2u_4,2v_4,2w_4\).  Hence every \(A\in\mathcal C_4\) is diagonal in this basis with eigenvalues
\[
4p_u,\quad4p_v,\quad4p_w,
\qquad p_u,p_v,p_w\geq0,\quad p_u+p_v+p_w=1.
\]
Put \(s=\rho^2\) and \(r=\max(p_v,p_w)\).  Allocating the component orthogonal to \(u_4\) to the larger of the last two eigen-directions gives
\[
q_\rho(A;S_4)
=4\max_{a^2\in[s,1]}\{p_u a^2+r(1-a^2)\}
=4\max\{p_u,\ p_us+r(1-s)\}.
\]
For fixed \(p_u=p\), the smallest possible \(r\) is \((1-p)/2\), attained by \(p_v=p_w=(1-p)/2\).  Therefore
\[
v^*(\rho;S_4)
=4\min_{0\leq p\leq1}
\max\left\{p,\ ps+\frac{(1-p)(1-s)}2\right\}.
\]
If \(s\leq1/3\), the minimum occurs at \(p=1/3\) and equals \(4/3\).  Indeed the two affine terms meet there, and moving to either side cannot lower their maximum.  If \(s\geq1/3\), the second affine term is nondecreasing in \(p\), so \(p=0\) is optimal and the value is \(2(1-s)\).  This proves
\[
v^*(\rho;S_4)=\min\left\{\frac43,\,2(1-\rho^2)\right\}.
\]
The choice \(p_u=p_v=p_w=1/3\) is complete randomization.  The choice \(p_u=0\), \(p_v=p_w=1/2\) is precisely the displayed law \(d_{\mathrm{pair},4}\), and direct averaging gives its displayed covariance \(A_{\mathrm{pair},4}\).  This covariance annihilates \(u_4\), so \(\kappa(S_4)=0\).  The strict-improvement set from the formula is \(\rho^2>1/3\).  The admissibility-frontier theorem consequently gives
\[
\gamma(S_4)=\frac13,
\qquad \rho^*(S_4)=\frac1{\sqrt3}.
\]

For general even \(n\), assign one treated and one control unit within every fixed pair, with independent fair orientations.  Every supported assignment is balanced and the distribution has mean zero.  If \(x\in S_{\mathrm{pair}}\), then
\[
z^\top x=\sum_{j=1}^{n/2}x_{2j-1}(z_{2j-1}+z_{2j})=0.
\]
Thus its covariance annihilates \(S_{\mathrm{pair}}\), proving \(\kappa(S_{\mathrm{pair}})=0<c_n\) and hence \(S_{\mathrm{pair}}\in\mathfrak A_n\).  At \(n=8\), perfect quality restricts \(\mu\) to this annihilated space, so \(v^*(1;S_{\mathrm{pair}})=0\) and, for \(M=1\),
\[
V^*(1;S_{\mathrm{pair}})=\frac{4}{8}\,0=0,
\qquad V_{\mathrm{CRD}}(1;S_{\mathrm{pair}})=\frac4{8-1}=\frac47.
\]
The exhaustive three-sign-pair calculation above is also the requested smallest exact stress test: it checks every balanced assignment at \(n=4\), including both sides of the switching boundary.

statements.statement:
Let \(z^{(1)},\ldots,z^{(m)}\) contain one representative from every balanced sign-pair, where \(m=|\mathcal Z_n|/2\), let \(\Delta_m\) be the probability simplex, and define \(A(a)=\sum_{j=1}^m a_jz^{(j)}z^{(j)\top}\).  If \(Q_H\) is any orthonormal basis matrix for \(H_n\), then the normalized unknown-quality regret has the exact finite-dimensional robust semidefinite representation
\[
\frac{n}{4M}R^*(n,S)
=\min_{a\in\Delta_m}\ \sup_{\substack{u\in H_n,\ \|u\|_2=1;\ b\in\Delta_m,\ \eta\geq0,\ \ell\in\mathbb R\\
\ell I_{n-1}-Q_H^\top\{A(b)+\eta P_S\}Q_H\succeq0}}
\left[u^\top A(a)u+\eta u^\top P_Su-\ell\right].
\]
Equivalently, its epigraph minimizes \(r\) over \(a\in\Delta_m\) subject to \(r\) being at least the displayed bracket for every tuple satisfying the displayed finite constraints.  Replacing the matrix inequality by its finitely many principal-minor inequalities and decomposing the resulting polynomial sign conditions gives finitely many spectral cells; their endpoints, the active-simplex faces, the generalized eigenvalue-crossing roots, and the compressed-spectrum endpoint \(\eta=\infty\) form a finite breakpoint description computable from a basis of \(S\) and \(n\).  Thus the value and an \(\varepsilon\)-optimal solution are computable by finite real-algebraic optimization, or numerically by certified subdivision and semidefinite optimization.

The outer minimum is attained.  Symmetrizing the optimal weights gives a design \(d_{\mathrm{reg}}\in\mathcal D_n\) satisfying
\[
\sup_{\rho\in[0,1]}
\left\{
\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal Y(\rho,M;S)}
\mathbb E_{d_{\mathrm{reg}}}[(\widehat\tau_{d_{\mathrm{reg}}}-\tau_n)^2]
-V^*(\rho;S)
\right\}=R^*(n,S),
\]
whereas the left side is at least \(R^*(n,S)\) for every single \(d\in\mathcal D_n\) selected without knowledge of \(\rho\).  Moreover, the support of an attaining design can always be chosen inside the support of the single \(\rho=0\) oracle design, namely complete randomization; hence it is contained in the union of supports of finitely many \(\rho\)-oracle designs.
statements.proof_tex:
For \(A\in\mathcal C_n\), abbreviate \(q_{\sqrt{s}}(A;S)\) by \(q_s(A)\) and \(v^*(\sqrt{s};S)\) by \(v(s)\).  If \(u\in H_n\) is a unit vector, put \(t(u)=u^\top P_Su\).  We first eliminate the continuum of quality-indexed spherical constraints by proving
\[
\sup_{0\leq s\leq1}\{q_s(A)-v(s)\}
=\sup_{\substack{u\in H_n\\\|u\|_2=1}}
\{u^\top Au-v(t(u))\}.
\tag{1}
\]
For the lower bound in \((1)\), fix \(u\) and take \(s=t(u)\); then \(q_s(A)\geq u^\top Au\).  For the upper bound, let \(u_s\) attain \(q_s(A)\) and put \(t=t(u_s)\geq s\).  The oracle value is nonincreasing because its adversary class shrinks as the quality lower bound increases, so \(v(s)\geq v(t)\).  Therefore
\[
q_s(A)-v(s)=u_s^\top Au_s-v(s)
\leq u_s^\top Au_s-v(t),
\]
which is bounded by the right side of \((1)\).

Now enumerate sign-pair representatives and write every \(B\in\mathcal C_n\) as \(A(b)\), \(b\in\Delta_m\).  The cone-lift scalar dual and the oracle minimization give, for \(t\in[0,1]\),
\[
v(t)=\inf_{\substack{b\in\Delta_m,\ \eta\geq0,\ \ell\in\mathbb R\\
\ell I_{n-1}-Q_H^\top\{A(b)+\eta P_S\}Q_H\succeq0}}
\{\ell-\eta t\}.
\tag{2}
\]
The matrix inequality says exactly that \(\ell\) dominates the largest eigenvalue on \(H_n\).  At \(t=1\), the infimum in \((2)\) may occur only as \(\eta\to\infty\); retaining an infimum is therefore essential.  Substituting \((2)\) into \((1)\) changes its negative infimum into a supremum and yields exactly the robust semidefinite representation in the theorem.  Taking the epigraph gives the displayed finite constraints.

Here is an explicit finite breakpoint procedure.  From a centered full-rank score basis, compute \(P_S\) and an orthonormal \(Q_H\), and enumerate the finite balanced sign-pairs.  Replace the sole matrix inequality in \((2)\) by nonnegativity of all principal minors.  Together with \(\|u\|_2^2=1\), the linear simplex equalities, and coordinate nonnegativity, this is a finite list of polynomial equalities and inequalities whose coefficients are entries of the score projector and the enumerated signs.  Recursively partition each coordinate line at the real roots of these polynomials and of their successive discriminants and resultants.  On each resulting sign-invariant cell, record the active simplex face and the eigenvalue branch determined by
\[
\det\!\left(\ell I_{n-1}-Q_H^\top\{A(b)+\eta P_S\}Q_H\right)=0.
\]
There are finitely many input polynomials of finite degree, so this recursive decomposition has finitely many cells after identically zero polynomials are passed to the next lower-dimensional stratum.  The projected cell endpoints in \(t=u^\top P_Su\), together with \(t=0,1\), are the required breakpoints.  Unbounded \(\eta\) is compactified by \(h=(1+\eta)^{-1}\); the cell \(h=0\) contributes only when \(t=1\), and its finite objective limit is the compressed eigenvalue \(\lambda_{\max}(P_SA(b)P_S\mid S)\), exactly as in the boundary part of the cone-lift proof.  Optimizing the polynomial objective over every cell and comparing finitely many cell optima computes the robust supremum and then the outer minimum.  For numerical score input, interval root isolation and semidefinite bounds give the stated \(\varepsilon\)-solution.  This construction uses only the score basis, \(n\), and the balanced signs.

It remains to establish attainment and the converse.  The function \(v(t)\) is continuous on \([0,1]\).  Indeed, for a fixed covariance, rotate the \(S\)- and \(S^\perp\)-components of a feasible unit vector to change its score energy; the Euclidean displacement tends uniformly to zero with the change in score energy, and
\[
|u^\top Au-w^\top Aw|\leq2\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}\|u-w\|_2\leq2n\|u-w\|_2,
\]
because \(A\succeq0\) and \(\operatorname{tr}(A)=n\).  This proves uniform continuity of each \(q_s(A)\), uniformly over \(A\in\mathcal C_n\), including the endpoints; minimization over the compact covariance hull preserves it.  Equation \((1)\) then expresses \(\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}(A;S)\) as the maximum of a jointly continuous function over the compact unit sphere.  It is continuous in \(A\).  Since \(\mathcal C_n\) is compact, an outer minimizer \(A_{\mathrm{reg}}\) exists.  Balanced-covariance realizability converts a convex representation of this matrix into a symmetrized \(d_{\mathrm{reg}}\in\mathcal D_n\).

The exact risk theorem gives, for every \(d\in\mathcal D_n\),
\[
\sup_{\rho\in[0,1]}
\left\{
\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal Y(\rho,M;S)}
\mathbb E_d[(\widehat\tau_d-\tau_n)^2]-V^*(\rho;S)
\right\}
=\frac{4M}{n}\Delta_{\mathrm{reg}}(A_d;S)
\geq R^*(n,S).
\]
Equality holds at \(A_{\mathrm{reg}}\), proving both attainability and the matching lower bound against every quality-agnostic design.

Finally, at \(\rho=0\), \(q_0(A;S)=\lambda_{\max}(A\mid H_n)\).  The trace bound gives \(q_0(A;S)\geq c_n\), while complete randomization has covariance \(c_nP_H\) and achieves equality.  It is therefore a \(\rho=0\) oracle design.  Its support is all of \(\mathcal Z_n\).  Any symmetrized representation of \(A_{\mathrm{reg}}\) uses only assignments in \(\mathcal Z_n\), so its support is contained in the support of this single oracle design.  This answers the final support question affirmatively, with one oracle support already sufficient.

sampling_model.design: A law \(d\in\mathcal D_n\) on exactly balanced sign assignments, selected using only the fixed score subspace \(S\).
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population of even size \(n\); there is no superpopulation draw.
sampling_model.treatment: Exactly \(n/2\) units receive treatment and \(n/2\) receive control; \(z\sim d\) is the only random object.
sampling_model.overlap: Mean-zero assignment, \(\mathbb E_d[z]=0\), gives marginal treatment probability \(1/2\) for every unit.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: None; the score-derived subspace \(S\) is a fixed design-stage primitive. The realized quality \(\rho_{\mu}(S)=\|P_S\mu\|_2/\|\mu\|_2\) depends on fixed potential outcomes, whereas \(\rho\in[0,1]\) is a free lower-bound parameter indexing oracle classes.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: The exact design-based mean squared error is a quadratic form in assignment covariance, while the Gram--Schmidt Walk supplies separate finite-sample balance and robustness guarantees.
Section 5 defines the mixed-strategy optimal design as worst-case-variance minimization for a specified structured conditional-mean class and gives a largest-eigenvalue form for ellipsoidal classes.
Page 5, Theorem 2 states that a symmetric Bernoulli correlation vector \(r\) is admissible if and only if \((1-r)/2\) lies in the cut polytope.
Matched-pair randomization is precision-optimal within the paper's stratified superpopulation design class.
A rerandomization threshold can trade observed balance against unobserved-covariate tail risk, conditional on unknown response quantities.
Euclidean rerandomization is minimax robust within a class of quadratic-form rerandomization criteria.
Gaussianized design optimization searches a restricted covariance family by local continuous optimization because the full binary covariance problem is cut-polytope hard.

tldr: An external prognostic score is useful for design only when its realized alignment \(\rho_{\mu}(S)=\|P_S\mu\|_2/\|\mu\|_2\) is high enough to compensate for the off-score risk created by restricted randomization; \(\rho\in[0,1]\) is the free lower-bound parameter indexing this oracle comparison. The paper derives the exact finite-population minimax SATE risk over every balanced mean-zero assignment law by lifting the score-quality shell to a rank-one-exact spectrahedron and optimizing over the true balanced sign covariance hull. The same reduction yields an attaining mixed design, a matching converse, an if-and-only-if admissibility certificate \(\kappa(S)<n/(n-1)\), and the score-matrix-computable threshold \(\rho^*(S)=\sqrt{\gamma(S)}\). A four-unit pair-score basis gives the worked values \(\kappa=0\), \(\gamma=1/3\), and \(\rho^*=1/\sqrt3\) with an explicit attaining sign-pair mixture. The remaining open object is the exact additive regret of one design chosen without knowing which lower bound is warranted.

project_justification.gap: Existing design theory either proves that complete randomization is minimax without predictive structure, optimizes a named restricted design under a chosen tuning parameter, or defines a generic mixed-strategy criterion and evaluates ellipsoidal outcome classes. It does not solve the nonellipsoidal lower score-energy shell, determine its exact fixed-count realizable covariance, or locate the transition below perfect prediction for an arbitrary external-score subspace.
project_justification.niche: The lower score-energy shell is strong enough to make minimax design nondegenerate but weak enough to represent score miscalibration and population shift. Its two quadratic constraints permit an exact lift, while exact balance forces the optimizer to remain in the balanced cut hull.
project_justification.fill: The proposal combines a rank-one-exact semidefinite adversary, minimax duality over balanced sign mixtures, and a compressed spectral certificate to deliver the value, attaining design, converse, admissibility dichotomy, and critical quality using only the score geometry available before randomization.

related_work: HarshawSavjeSpielmanZhang2024 supplies the design-based covariance identity and motivates tuning by predictive quality, but Section 8 of its supplement states that the relevant quality ratio is unavailable at design time. Kallus2018OptimalBalance develops the zero-sum mixed-design architecture and the no-free-lunch benchmark under unstructured outcomes. Kallus2021Randomization, Section 5, defines the generic mixed-strategy optimal design for a specified conditional-mean class and gives a largest-eigenvalue criterion for an ellipsoidal class. The theorem-level delta is not the generic existence of an optimal mixture: it is the rank-one-exact solution of the nonellipsoidal lower score-energy shell, the exact saddle program over the fixed-count balanced cut hull, recovery of an attaining sign-pair law, and the if-and-only-if quality frontier. HuberMaric2019, p. 5, Theorem 2, identifies symmetric Bernoulli correlation vectors with a cut-polytope image; it neither imposes fixed treatment counts nor studies causal risk. Bai2022MatchedPairs gives a scalar-prognosis endpoint within stratified superpopulation designs, not a converse over all fixed-population balanced laws. KapelnerKriegerSklarAzriel2022 shows that rerandomization tuning depends on unknown response features, motivating oracle-relative regret. SchulerWalshHallWalshFisher2022 documents why externally trained score quality can deteriorate under domain shift. SchindlBranson2024 compares quadratic-form rerandomization rules but explicitly leaves comparison with other design classes outside its scope. GuoLiangToulis2025 uses a Gaussianized covariance subclass and local optimization because the full binary covariance geometry is hard; the present exact program keeps the full discrete hull and accepts exponential worst-case computation.
technical_internal_limitation: For \(n=8\) and \(S=S_{\mathrm{pair}}\), the matched-pair design has zero risk on vectors constant within pairs, yet exact enumeration also produces a fixed mean vector with within-pair variation on which its risk is \(1.75\) times the complete-randomization risk. Thus \(V^*(1;S_{\mathrm{pair}})=0\) does not justify matched pairs at lower quality, and no theorem may infer global dominance from perfect-score performance.
honest_scope: The finite-population oracle value, attaining design, full-class converse, admissibility dichotomy, threshold formula, computability by finite enumeration, and endpoint reductions are theorem targets. Polynomial-time computation is not claimed; the balanced cut hull can require exponentially many assignments. The exact finite-breakpoint form of \(R^*(n,S)\), its attaining quality-agnostic design, and any asymptotic growing-rank theory remain open. The sanity reduction \(S=H_n\) returns complete randomization for every quality. For the four-unit pair-score basis, the exact switch from complete randomization to the displayed balanced sign-pair mixture occurs at \(\rho=1/\sqrt3\), while general \(S_{\mathrm{pair}}\) returns the zero-risk matched-pair endpoint at \(\rho=1\).
